Dataset project page

A real-world strawberry dataset for detection and keypoint estimation

This dataset provides instance-level annotations for strawberries captured in greenhouse environments. Each annotated fruit combines a bounding box, five anatomical keypoints, a ripeness label, and an occlusion label.

01

Overview

Abstract

Strawberry perception in field conditions is complicated by foliage, uneven illumination, overlapping fruit, maturity variation, and partial visibility. These conditions are retained in the dataset so that models can be studied under realistic visual complexity.

The annotation structure supports several related computer-vision tasks within one instance record. Bounding boxes define object extent, five keypoints encode landmark geometry, and two categorical attributes describe ripeness and occlusion.

Dataset scope

  • Real greenhouse imagery rather than isolated objects
  • Instance localization and landmark supervision
  • Ripeness and visibility attributes
  • Suitable for multi-task agricultural perception studies
02

Method

Annotation protocol

Each strawberry instance is represented by a compact set of spatial and categorical annotations. The table summarizes the public schema without inferring unpublished dataset statistics.

Signal Representation Intended use Per instance
Localization Axis-aligned bounding box Object detection and instance localization 1 box
Geometry Anatomical landmark coordinates Keypoint estimation and shape reasoning 5 points
Ripeness Categorical maturity label Visual grading and attribute recognition 1 label
Occlusion Categorical visibility label Robustness analysis under partial visibility 1 label
Annotation record { bbox, keypoints[5], ripeness, occlusion }
